sonnet.problem: Card 6 already asks whether David keeps his trust when war breaks out. Its question says he 'will keep his ___' in the face of an army, so card 7's True/False ('his heart will be afraid') is answered by it. Card 7 also re-asks the same point from the same verse (no fear despite the army).
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word from the line ('gaze on the ___ of the LORD'). Nothing earlier in the stop points to 'beauty' over 'riches' or 'power', so the pick comes down to luck or to knowing the wording.
sonnet.rule: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
